BCR-induced ROS production is derived from both NADPH oxidases and the mitochondria and that ROS produced by these sources play a critical role at later stages of activation in promoting sustained BCR-induced signaling and proliferation.
the BCR-induced production of ROS plays a critical role in the activation and proliferation of primary B cells in vitro and in the generation of Ab responses in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reactive oxygen species in B cell activation and proliferation in response to antigen.
the role of ROS in the activation and differentiation of B cells.
the role of reactive oxygen species in the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCR-induced generation of ROS is critical for the later stages of the BCR signaling and activation of B cells, but is not required for the initial stages of BCR activation.
BCR stimulation induces the rapid production of reactive oxygen species in primary murine B cells that occurs within minutes and is maintained for at least several hours after receptor stimulation.
the production of reactive oxygen species downstream of the B cell receptor is derived from at leas t two cellular sources and plays an important role at the later stage of B cell activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of reactive oxygen species downstream of the B cell receptor (BCR) is derived from at two distinct cellular sources (NADPH oxidase and mitochondria) and plays a critical and essential role in BCR signaling, B cell proliferation, and B cell responses to antigen (Ag).
B cells have two sources of ROS production, NADPH oxidases and mitochondria.
ROS are critical for B cell activation and proliferation in response to B cell receptor stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BCR-induced ROS production is critical for the later stages of activation, proliferation, and differentiation of B cells, but not for early signaling.
ROS production in B cells is not only a source of oxidative stress but also an important signaling molecule in the activation of the B cell response.

the B cell receptor (BCR) is not only the sensor that detects and responds to Ag, but it is also the initiator of a complex series of signaling pathways that regulate many aspects of B cell activation and function, including the production of reactive oxygen species.
